extracted.intended_audience: historical demographers, anthropologists, and historians studying California Native populations
extracted.subtask_description: Estimating and reconstructing aboriginal population sizes for the San Joaquin Valley (primarily c.1770–1860) using historical, ethnographic, and administrative sources, with area-by-area breakdowns and methodological corrections for undercounts and decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangulation of three primary data bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use three primary bodies of data to estimate population: (1) contemporary American counts and reports (1848–1852) by settlers, commissioners, and officers; (2) modern ethnographic studies (Kroeber, Merriam, Gifford, etc.) based on informants (c.1900–1940); (3) Spanish and Mexican historical records (diaries, reports, baptism lists, mission censuses) for pre‑1770 conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine and cross-check these sources appropriate to the target period (contemporary counts + ethnography for c.1850; Spanish/Mexican records for pre‑1770). Recognize each source's temporal and methodological limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal appropriateness of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish time periods explicitly (pre‑1770, 1770–1840, c.1850) and use the data sources that are relevant for each period; the demography can be determined with some accuracy at two stages: around 1850 and just before Spanish entrance (pre‑1770).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat estimates for earlier periods as direct evidence for 1850 (and vice versa). Adjust interpretation if a source clearly refers to an earlier/later date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define geographic boundaries and mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: State explicit boundaries of the study region (north bank of upper Bay/Sacramento River to Tehachapi; include Sierra Nevada west slope where permanent habitation occurred) and delineate smaller numbered areas on maps for reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit that area divisions are somewhat arbitrary; maps and numbered habitat areas aid comparison but may not coincide exactly with tribal boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize and weigh estimates by methodological reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate crude broad generalizations (subjective impressions/guesses) from semi‑estimates or counts based on attempted enumeration; prefer methods that provide measurable bases (village lists, administrative distributions) over unsupported large guesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discard or downweight very high values that are 'mere guesses' or apply to a different period; favor village‑based or administrative checks when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of administrative records as independent checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use non‑population administrative data (e.g., vaccination vouchers, blanket distribution lists, treaties stating numbers to receive blankets) to check or infer population totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert such records into population estimates using stated program rules (e.g., 1 blanket per person over 15) and demographic assumptions (see age‑distribution criterion). Treat differences between administrative tallies (vaccinations vs. blanket claims) as informative about undercounting or nonparticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct for undercounting in participation records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that counts based on voluntary participation (e.g., vaccinations) undercount the true population relative to entitlement lists (e.g., blanket distributions), and correct vaccination totals upward using ratios derived from other records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ryer's vaccination totals (6,154 from Stanislaus to Tulare) were increased to match blanket distribution implications; adjust local vaccination subsamples by the observed ratio of blanket claims to vaccinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume demographic ratios for conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: When administrative programs specify distributions to subgroups (e.g., 'one blanket apiece for every person over fifteen years of age'), assume demographic proportions (the author assumes persons over 15 are at least 80% of total population) to convert program counts to total population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make and state explicit assumptions (e.g., % of population >15). Use conservative assumptions and explain sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area‑by‑area (restricted areas) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Break the entire region into smaller physiographic/river‑based units (Stanislaus, Tuolumne, Merced, etc.) and estimate population for each unit rather than relying on broad aggregates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps capture overlooked groups, allows local source triangulation, and enables use of village lists and local administrative records more effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ethnographic village lists and per‑village averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ethnographers' village lists (Kroeber, Merriam, Gifford) and average persons per village (e.g., Gifford's average of ~21 persons per permanent village) to estimate populations by multiplying village counts by an appropriate per‑village average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate permanent vs temporary camps; apply local appropriate per‑village averages (may vary by region and indicate decline if averages are small). Prefer village‑list based estimates when compiled carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust per‑village size for demographic decline
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret unusually small village population figures (many villages with 10–15 persons) as evidence of rapid population decline and adjust expectations about what constitutes a 'normal' settlement size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On this evidence, do not assume precontact normal village sizes when village counts indicate severe attrition; use observed averages (even if low) for the relevant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiographic comparators and density extrapolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare physiographically similar river systems to compute village density (villages per river mile) and use the mean density to estimate village counts on less documented rivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure river length from maps and apply mean villages/mile (example: mean 0.34 villages/river mile) to infer likely village numbers where ethnographic coverage is sparse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer certain source types when averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple estimates exist, compute averages but give preference to more reliable sources (e.g., carefully compiled village lists) rather than crude numerical averages of all claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: crude numerical average for Stanislaus‑Tuolumne was ~2,070, but village lists suggested ~1,800, so the author preferred the latter and set 2,000 as approximation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for reservation/administrative scope limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that official counts by agents/commissioners often include only those incorporated into the reservation system and thus omit many remnant groups; treat reservation counts as lower bounds, not totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust upward for uncounted groups living outside reservations, particularly in remote foothills and plains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust for informant memory and informant generation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When using ethnographic informants' recollections, account for the informant's age and likely memory horizon (e.g., a 75‑year‑old informant born ~1840 cannot reliably report pre‑1840 population figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use informant data cautiously for dates beyond their direct experience; supplement with parents' recollections when available and note uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle mobile/seasonal settlement systems carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not equate the number of named hamlets or 'places' directly to static population counts when the culture practiced frequent household moves (e.g., Western Mono hamlets where families moved every few years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze turnover, permanence, and household mobility before translating site counts into population; use ethnohistorical descriptions to infer effective population per site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative settlement size evidence to set per‑village averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrate per‑village population estimates using settlement sizes reported in the literature for nearby or similar tribes (e.g., Johnston's average of 125 per rancheria on lower Tuolumne; Wessels' reports) and reconcile conflicting indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different comparators disagree, choose an intermediate, justifying why extremes are likely too high or too low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about uncertainty and round to reflect it
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide ranges and round off to even numbers (e.g., round village‑based totals to 2,500) to reflect uncertainty and the rough nature of estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reasons for choosing a rounded figure over a precise calculated mean; give upper/lower plausible bounds when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and correct for double‑counting and ambiguous tribal names
rubrics_metrics.description: When administrative or vaccination lists contain duplicate or indeterminate tribal/rancheria names, correct counts by estimating number of distinct tribal entities and adjusting per‑tribe averages accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ryer's lists had duplicate/unrecognizable names; the author reduced average per‑tribe population from 232 to 200 to allow for such issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret pioneer/settler reports with caution for temporal bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that pioneer accounts (Savage, Gilbert, Mason) may refer to pre‑Gold Rush conditions and thus overstate populations for c.1850; check whether an author explicitly or implicitly refers to earlier periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such temporal mismatch is suspected, do not directly use the higher figures for the target date without adjustment.
